samples.question: The picture shows small dark gray squares of one common size (the stones), one larger dark green square (the pad), and three coloured squares: an orange flag, a purple flag and a blue flag. No two squares touch. Two squares are linked when the clear white gap between them is narrower than one stone is wide, and they are not linked when that gap is at least as wide as a stone. Linking chains: the pad reaches a square if you can get from the pad to it through a run of linked squares, hopping only over gaps narrower than a stone. Exactly one of the three flags is cut off from the pad: the run of stones leading to that flag is interrupted by a single gap at least as wide as a stone, so no hopping route reaches it. The other two flags are reachable. Stone count, run length, how far a flag sits from the pad and the direction of a run say nothing about the answer, and stones that are linked to nothing are still ordinary stones. Which flag is cut off from the green pad? Answer orange, purple, or blue.
